Quick Reference: Gamma Transition Selection Rules

This document provides a fast lookup for nuclear electromagnetic transitions based on multipolarity ($L$), spin change ($\Delta J$), and parity change ($\Delta \pi$).

1. Multipolarity to $\Delta J$ and $\Delta \pi$

Use this table to determine allowed transitions when the multipolarity is known.

  • Angular Momentum Rule: $|\Delta J| \leq L \leq J_i + J_f$
  • Prohibition: Transition order $L$ cannot be zero ($0 \to 0$ photon emission is strictly forbidden).

| Type | Order (L) | Allowed absolute spin change (|ΔJ|) | Parity change? | Parity transformation (initial ↔ final) | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | | E1 | $1$ | 0 or 1 | Yes | Parity change: initial ≠ final | | M1 | $1$ | 0 or 1 | No | Parity unchanged: initial = final | | E2 | $2$ | 0, 1 or 2 | No | Parity unchanged: initial = final | | M2 | $2$ | 0, 1 or 2 | Yes | Parity change: initial ≠ final | | E3 | $3$ | 0, 1, 2 or 3 | Yes | Parity change: initial ≠ final | | M3 | $3$ | 0, 1, 2 or 3 | No | Parity unchanged: initial = final | | E4 | $4$ | 0–4 | No | Parity unchanged: initial = final | | M4 | $4$ | 0–4 | Yes | Parity change: initial ≠ final |

2. $\Delta J$ and $\Delta \pi$ to Multipolarity

Use this table to find the lowest-order (most probable) multipolarities given experimental spin-parity changes.

  • Competition: Generally, the lowest allowed transition order $L$ dominates the decay.
  • Collective Enhancements: E2 transitions often compete with M1 (mixed transitions) due to collective nuclear deformation.
  • Suppression: Higher‑order multipoles are suppressed by many orders of magnitude relative to the lowest allowed multipole and are usually negligible unless nuclear structure strongly enhances them.

| Spin Change (|ΔJ|) | No parity change (same parity) | Parity change (opposite parity) | | :---: | :--- | :--- | | 0 | M1 (E2 mixing possible) | E1 (M2 negligible) | | 1 | M1 + E2 (Commonly mixed) | E1 (M2 negligible) | | 2 | E2 (M3 negligible) | M2 + E3 (Mixed) | | 3 | M3 (E4 negligible) | E3 (M4 negligible) | | 4 | E4 | M4 |

Critical note: For J_i = J_f = 0 (0⁺ → 0⁺), single‑photon emission is forbidden. Such transitions proceed via electric monopole (E0) processes — typically internal conversion or, if the transition energy exceeds 2m_ec^2, e⁺e⁻ pair emission. E0 requires ΔJ = 0 and no parity change.

3. General Selection Laws

  • Angular Momentum Conservation: The emitted photon carries a total angular momentum $L$, where: $$ |J_i - J_f| \leq L \leq J_i + J_f $$
  • Parity Selection Rules:
    • Electric transitions ($EL$): $\Delta \pi = (-1)^L$. Parity is inverted if $L$ is odd.
    • Magnetic transitions ($ML$): $\Delta \pi = (-1)^{L+1}$. Parity is inverted if $L$ is even.
